verdict.rationale: Mastra is a TypeScript framework whose tools must be defined with zod `inputSchema` and `outputSchema`. Workflow steps are described as type-safe, and structured output is schema-shaped. A community user also calls it best in class for TypeScript. Explicit documentation that these types and schemas surface a coding agent's mistakes at build or compile time is not present; that part is only implied by the TypeScript stack. missing for 10: explicit docs on compile-time type inference and errors from schemas, evidence of build-time (vs runtime) validation catching agent mistakes, hands-on corroboration of the agent self-correction loop

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can rely on strict typing and schema validation so a coding agent catches its own mistakes at build time

citations.quote: tools MUST be defined via `createTool()` with `id`, `description`, `inputSchema` (zod), `execute()`
Workflow steps can call agents to use LLM reasoning or call tools for type-safe logic.
Mastra is a TypeScript framework for building AI agents and applications.
Mastra is best in class for working with TypeScript.
